title: x
Engine specifications in Quint: st → groups → distributed
description: Formal specs of Dizzy engines. Semantics are defined at the weakest topology (async, arbitrary lag); the monolith (st) is the zero-lag degenerate case. Target property (dizzy/docs/explanation/topology.md): same feature-file + any rule-6-legal topology ⇒ byte-identical models. Spec is parametric over an abstract feature (procedures/projections/policies/queries + their reads/writes), not per feature-file.

title: Spec 1: single-threaded engine (st) — Engine.ingest as one atomic step
description: Quint module modelling a hybrid group: durable command queue + append-only log + models as folds. ingest = append → fold → commit → run policies, atomic. Parametric over an abstract feature. Invariants: models == fold(log) after every step; every policy-dispatched command is causally after its trigger event; determinism (same script ⇒ same log).
closeReason: specs/st.qnt: 5 invariants hold under quint run (1000 traces × 20 steps); rejection + welcome witnesses reachable

title: Spec 2: consumer groups — per-group cursor + lane, fold-claim-fold-run-fold cycle
description: Generalise Spec 1 to N groups each with its own cursor and lane; interleave arbitrarily. Encode placement rules 1,3,6 as a predicate over topology×feature. Property: rule-6-legal topology refines st (byte-identical models). Expect rule-6-violating layouts to produce the 'reads empty model, dispatches nothing' divergence.
closeReason: specs/groups.qnt: claim/execute split, rewind, guarded; T1 rule6⇒causeFolded∧freshDispatch and T2 singleGroupIsSt hold; witnessClaimWindow shows rule-6-legal stale reads are real

title: Spec 3: fault model — per-device substrate, sharded policy groups, element failure, lane-file loss
description: Add message loss, cursor rewind to zero, at-least-once redelivery. Properties: doorbell drops cost latency not work; cursor loss is safe iff commands dedupe on deterministic ids and procedures guard; sharded event-only policy groups redeliver only one shard's tail.

title: Trace validation of TopologyEngine against engine.qnt (a real, OS-scheduled run checked as a Quint behaviour)
description:
Retargeted from st (removed from DIZZY main) to spec/specs/engine.qnt, the spec of engine/src/dizzy_topology_engine.

DONE (2026-10-14): state-level conformance. engine/tests/test_spec_conformance.py runs the real TopologyEngine on random graphs, random rule-3 placements, and an in-process crash at EVERY claim/append/enqueue point, then evaluates _spec.py (a port of engine.qnt's invariants) on the store.

DONE (2026-10-14): spec-to-engine, step level (model-based testing). engine/tests/test_mbt.py generates traces with quint run --mbt from two instances of the spec (engine; engineNarrow, a one-wide pool) and _mbt.py replays each action on a real engine held at its transactions (DrivenEngine pauses after claim, append+ack, each enqueue, each fold, the cursor). After every step one abstraction function maps store + memory to the spec's variables and must equal the trace's state. Catches mutants the state-level suite misses: claim order, recovery-first, pool capacity, the old batch collect.

REMAINING: the other direction, for runs the spec did not drive: real ProcessPoolExecutor scheduling and the crash sweep. Record the abstract state at every DrivenEngine pause of such a run and check each consecutive pair is an engine.qnt step (for example a generated quint run test whose schedule is the recorded action list, or an ITF trace evaluated against the invariants).

title: Monotonicity classifier over the feature graph (CALM)
description: Label each edge monotone / non-monotone. Non-monotone reads force co-location (aggregate boundary, = rule 6); read-your-writes gets a watermark token. Output feeds topology validation.

title: Adversarial-scheduler engine in Python + Hypothesis stateful tests
description: Partly covered (2026-10-14): test_spec_conformance.py sweeps every crash point in-process and adds a second random crash per reopen, over random graphs and placements. The adversarial SCHEDULER now exists: test_mbt.py's ManualPool finishes pool jobs in the order the spec's trace chooses (and fails the ones it fails), so completion order is the model checker's choice, not the OS's. Remaining: Hypothesis stateful tests with shrinking (or shrinking of failing Quint traces), if the MBT traces' coverage turns out thin anywhere.

title: Design: close the claim→run window in GroupWorker (or accept causeFolded as the guarantee)
description: groups.qnt witnessClaimWindow: a rule-6-legal split can run a procedure against a model behind the tail because groups.py:419-426 has no lock between the middle fold_to_tail() and execute(). Options: (a) re-check tail after claim and re-fold under a lock; (b) restate topology.md 'byte-identical models' as 'model committed through the cause' (groups.py:27-29). Decision belongs in dizzy, not here.

title: Spec 3a: own appends folded ahead of earlier foreign entries
description: The worker's execute() runs ingest, folding the group's own events inline before earlier foreign entries its cursor has not reached. Invisible under set semantics; may matter once model contents are ordered.

title: Spec 3b: per-device substrate replicas
description: groups.qnt assumes one shared sqla DB. topology.md describes per-process models. Model substrate[h] per group; rule 6 witnesses change meaning.

title: Spec 3c: element raising mid-emission (partial block) + host put interleaving inside a cascade
description: Both excluded from st.qnt by header. blocksWellFormed will need a 'partial block then recovery' form.

title: Spec 3d: sharded event-only policy groups (k/N cursors) and lane-file loss
description: topology.md 'What workers: N buys' and the 'new hazard' paragraph.

title: Design: 'procedures guard' is a graph rule — only guardable procedures can be exactly-once
description: st.qnt/groups.qnt: the only guard an application can implement is 'my own earlier block is in a model I read' (seesOwnBlock). So exactly-once under at-least-once delivery holds iff guardable(g,p) = reads(p) ∩ {m : folds(m) ∩ emits(p) ≠ ∅} ≠ ∅, AND rule 6 (the model is folded by p's own group before it claims). witnessUnguardable / witnessGuardMissed are reachable. topology.md:347-351 should state this as a validator rule, or the generator should emit the guard.

title: Spec 2 revision: per-pair causeFoldedLocal, ack/crash pair instead of redeliver-any
description: Two deferred re-review items: state T1 per co-located (reader, model) pair rather than global rule 6; model recovery as ack/crash (only the in-flight row redelivers).

title: Re-found consumer groups on the Simple Engine store; groups.qnt is the design spec
description: v2's groups.py (per-group cursors, doorbell transports) was never wired even on v2, and its base engine is gone. Re-found it on the Simple Engine store (per-group cursors beside the store's own) with spec/specs/groups.qnt revised to the new transaction boundaries, as engine.qnt was for st. Topology fields transport/cursors/max_in_flight are validated but not executed until then.

title: Decide: topology retry: field vs Simple Engine §11.2 (no automatic retry)
description: topology.yaml (from v2) has a per-group retry: policy with backoff and dead_letter. Simple Engine spec §11.2 says no automatic retry (host calls retry), and DIZZY's rule says a retry is a reaction and must be a declared policy. Drop the field, or make it something the build validates and the host acts on. The engine ignores it today; engine.qnt models host retry only.

title: Profiler: read Simple Engine trace spans instead of v2 JsonlBusSink records
description: topology/src/dizzy_topology/profiler.py parses JsonlBusSink records, which nothing on DIZZY main produces. The Simple Engine writes telemetry/*.jsonl spans with per-element duration_ms; the topology engine adds dizzy.lane and dizzy.procedure_ms on pool units. Port the profiler's input onto those.

title: Scale ladder: include engine.qnt
description: spec/scale/gen.py copies st.qnt and groups.qnt verbatim into each generated universe; engine.qnt is not on the ladder yet. Its proofs at the base size: depth 3/4/5/6 in 11 s/19 s/44 s/3.7 min.

title: Read-only models: consider a feature-level declaration in DIZZY (ModelDef.read_only)
description: Read-only (reference) models are declared in topology.yaml (read_only_models) because half of 'never updates' is a deployment promise: nothing outside the event stream writes the model while the engine runs. The other half (no projection folds it) is a fact of the feature, and foogle_shindig's gronk_values description already anticipates a 'read_only: true' annotation on the model. If DIZZY grew ModelDef.read_only, generation could emit read-only adapter handles (a sqla session on a mode=ro connection) and refuse a projection into one at feat validation time; the topology would then only add the deployment promise. Needs a DIZZY change (just dizzy-dev), so it is a decision for DIZZY's tracker.

title: Rule 7 at build time: multi-feat input (core + plugins) and order-independent declarations
description: engine.qnt shows a reopen refolds a model fed by two domains' stores out of append order, and that rule 7 (such a model is declared order-independent) prevents decisions on a reordered model (reopenReordersTest, foldsInLogOrder, readsInLogOrder; README 'The reopen harm'). Enforce it at build time: dizzy-topology check/place take a core feat plus its plugins (an event's store is its emitting procedure's domain), and refuse a model folded from more than one store unless declared order-independent. Where the declaration lives (topology.yaml beside read_only_models, or the feat) is open. Alternative fix (DIZZY's call, Simple Engine §11 Q3): record cross-store append order durably so a rebuild replays it.
